decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Living Systems and Diversity
decks.description: Explain biological organization and evidence.

includes: Introductory cellular, organismal, and evolutionary representations
excludes: Molecular mechanisms and quantitative population theory

practice: Compare organisms and critique explanations using observational evidence.

outcomes.description: Distinguish major bacterial, archaeal, and eukaryotic lineages using cellular and lifecycle traits.
Explain inheritance, variation, selection, and information flow without teleological reasoning.
Distinguish observations, hypotheses, mechanisms, and comparative evidence in biological claims.
Compare cellular organization, biological scales, energy use, and feedback in living systems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Quantitative Foundations
decks.description: Use the common language of quantitative models.

includes: Computational algebra, trigonometry, coordinates, and quantitative notation
excludes: Calculus and axiomatic vector spaces

practice: Solve multistep quantitative problems and check units and limiting cases.

outcomes.description: Manipulate fractions, equations, inequalities, powers, and complex numbers correctly.
Translate between formulas and graphs for polynomial, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions.
Calculate lengths, angles, coordinates, and elementary vector operations.
Convert units and interpret ratios, scales, rounding, and significant figures.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Foundations
decks.description: Represent matter and account for chemical change.

includes: Chemical notation, quantitative reaction accounting, and atomic periodicity
excludes: Quantum derivations and detailed bonding theory

practice: Solve multistep composition and reaction-accounting problems.

outcomes.description: Interpret atomic, ionic, molecular, and phase notation and determine chemical composition.
Explain isotopes, electronic configurations, and periodic trends using introductory atomic models.
Balance reactions and calculate mole, mass, concentration, yield, and limiting-reagent relationships.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Foundations
decks.description: Express, execute, and debug computational procedures.

includes: One general-purpose language and transferable programming concepts
excludes: Machine-level memory management and large-system architecture

practice: Write increasingly substantial programs from specifications without template copying.

outcomes.description: Design functions and recursive procedures with explicit inputs, outputs, and contracts.
Manipulate structured collections and files and distinguish representation choices.
Develop tests, diagnose failures, and revise programs systematically.
Trace variables, expressions, control flow, types, and program state.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Single-Variable Calculus
decks.description: Model continuous change and accumulation.

includes: Computational calculus and power-series approximation
excludes: Proof-level real analysis

practice: Solve unfamiliar modeling and approximation problems with error checks.

outcomes.description: Differentiate compositions and solve sensitivity, optimization, and related-rate problems.
Apply the fundamental theorem, substitution, parts, and improper integration.
Evaluate limits and use continuity to justify local models.
Test sequence and series convergence and bound Taylor approximation errors.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Proof, Sets, and Relations
decks.description: Construct and critique mathematical arguments.

includes: Elementary formal reasoning and proof writing
excludes: Metalogical completeness and axiomatic set theory

practice: Write proofs and diagnose invalid arguments.

outcomes.description: Translate quantified statements and distinguish implication, equivalence, and negation.
Construct direct, contrapositive, contradiction, and induction proofs with counterexamples.
Use sets, functions, equivalence relations, orders, and countability arguments.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Physical Modeling and Measurement
decks.description: Translate physical situations into testable models.

includes: Units, estimation, representation grammar, and measurement concepts
excludes: Statistical uncertainty propagation and advanced instrumentation

practice: Estimate unfamiliar quantities and design simple measurement checks.

outcomes.description: Construct dimensionally consistent models and estimate scales and limiting behavior.
Distinguish resolution, random variation, systematic error, and model discrepancy.
Translate among diagrams, coordinates, vectors, graphs, and operationally defined quantities.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Bonding and Molecular Structure
decks.description: Explain molecular shape and physical properties.

includes: Conceptual electronic structure and molecular representations
excludes: Ab initio electronic-structure derivations

practice: Build competing structural models and defend property predictions.

outcomes.description: Compare Lewis, valence-bond, and molecular-orbital models and their predictive limits.
Predict molecular geometry, polarity, resonance, and bond-order trends.
Relate intermolecular interactions to phase behavior, solubility, and molecular association.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Laboratory Foundations
decks.description: Perform basic chemical work safely and traceably.

includes: Supervised laboratory entry skills and records
excludes: Unsupervised hazardous synthesis and advanced instrument operation

practice: Complete supervised technique assessments and maintain an auditable laboratory notebook.

outcomes.description: Prepare solutions and record calibrated mass and volume measurements with traceable uncertainty.
Perform basic filtration, extraction, crystallization, and distillation and explain separation principles.
Assess hazards, compatibility, exposure controls, waste streams, and emergency procedures.

decks.subject: computer-science

includes: Formal-language theory and computability proofs
excludes: Resource-bounded complexity and advanced recursion theory

practice: Construct machines and grammars and write impossibility proofs.

outcomes.description: Construct finite automata and regular expressions and prove closure and nonregularity results.
Relate context-free grammars, pushdown automata, parsing, and language limitations.
Construct Turing-machine and equivalent computation models and distinguish decision from recognition.
Prove undecidability using reductions, diagonalization, and Rice-type arguments.

decks.subject: computer-science

excludes: Semiconductor fabrication and operating-system memory policy

practice: Build simulated circuits and analyze assembly and processor traces.

outcomes.description: Construct Boolean, combinational, and sequential circuits and explain binary and numeric encodings.
Trace machine instructions, registers, addressing, and assembly-level control flow.
Analyze caches, locality, memory traffic, and processor performance using explicit cost models.
Explain datapaths, control, pipelining, hazards, and instruction-level parallelism.

decks.subject: computer-science

outcomes.description: Compare architectural tradeoffs and plan evolution, deployment, maintenance, and technical-debt reduction.
Use version control, reviews, issue tracking, and reproducible builds in team workflows.
Design cohesive modules and interfaces using abstraction, encapsulation, and dependency control.
Translate stakeholder needs into requirements, contracts, and acceptance criteria.
Develop unit, integration, property-based, and regression tests and diagnose failures.
